sentiment.label: neutral

market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets positive: S&P 500 +0.81%, STOXX 600 +1.36%, Nikkei +0.38%. Rates: US 10Y Yield -0.67% to 4.41%, BTP 10Y stable. Commodities: Gold +2.86%, Oil -2.63%. Currencies: EUR/USD +0.39% to 1.17.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.38%, Shanghai in rialzo dell'1.17%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.81%, il VIX è in calo dell'1.61%. Il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0.37%, mentre l'oro è in rialzo del 2.86% a 4685.9 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è in calo del 2.63% a 106.98 dollari. I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani a 10 anni sono in calo dello 0.67% al 4.41%.

La Banca Centrale dell'Australia ha alzato i tassi d'interesse, mossa che va contro la tendenza globale. Il Regno Unito ha visto un aumento dei costi di finanziamento a lungo termine al livello più alto dal 1998 Inoltre, India e Russia hanno firmato un patto che consente la presenza di truppe e navi da guerra sul territorio dell'altro.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari, con una variazione del +0,59%. I flussi ETF giornalieri netti sono stati di +73,9 milioni di dollari, segno di un interesse ancora presente. Questo movimento conferma l'attenzione degli investitori verso Bitcoin in un contesto di mercato volatile.

Per quanto riguarda le altcoin, Ethereum scende dello 0,43% a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana guadagna il 3,20% a ottantasette dollari e sessantatre centesimi. BNB invece registra un +1,58% a seicentotrentasette dollari e sessantuno centesimi.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 46, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.38%, Shanghai up 1.17%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.81%, the VIX is down 1.61%. The Dollar Index is down 0.37%, while gold is up 2.86% to $4,685.9 per ounce. Brent crude oil is down 2.63% to $106.98 US 10-year Treasury yields are down 0.67% to 4.41%. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates, a move that goes against the global trend. The UK saw an increase in long-term financing costs to the highest level since 1998 Additionally, India and Russia signed a pact that allows for the presence of troops and warships on each other's territory. No major macroeconomic data releases today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above eighty thousand dollars, with a variation of +0.59%. Daily net ETF flows were +$73.9 million, a sign of continued interest. This movement confirms investors' attention towards Bitcoin in a volatile market context. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum down 0.43% to $2,300, while Solana gains 3.2% to $87.63 BNB registers a +1.58% to $637.61 The Fear & Greed Index is at 46, in Fear zone, suggests caution for investors. We are awaiting economic data releases today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

Earlier, India successfully tested the capability to deploy multiple independently targetable warheads from a single missile. articles.title: UAE’s Shock Exit Leaves OPEC Weakened and the Global Oil Order Rewritten
articles.snippet: Before 1 May, the once-mighty Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) had 12 members, but with the departure of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) at the start of the month, it has 11. These comprise Algeria, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela, together accounting for around 33% of the world’s crude oil output, about 46% of its total petroleum traded internationally, and roughly 73% of its proven oil reserves. Back when it was founded in 1960, these…

articles.title: US Senators Push to Reinstate Russian Oil Sanctions
articles.snippet: A group of 14 Senate Democrats is pressing the Trump administration to reinstate sanctions on Russian oil after a temporary waiver tied to the Iran war. In a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the lawmakers argued that the policy allows additional revenue to flow to Moscow, at a time when oil prices are already elevated. The administration first eased sanctions in mid-March after the Strait of Hormuz disruption tightened global supply and pushed prices sharply higher. The 30-day waiver, initially set to expire April 11, has been extended…
